clue.text: Chronic disorder remains to beset tense old woman

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so the remains wrap around the tense

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
MA is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A long-term illness besieges a nervous elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: This breathing complaint is a classic example of a long-lasting medical condition.

clue.text: Relish receiving current bringer of delivery

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the relish holds the current

parts.note: to savour is to relish
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys an electrical supply brought by a deliveryman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer delivers people from danger, so one who brings deliverance fits.

clue.text: Badger runs repeatedly into grass

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the doubled letter enters the grass

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: repeatedly means the abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A badger dashes again and again through the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to pester or harass someone persistently.

clue.text: Blame I dismissed, having taken vehicle in historic African site

indicators.note: having taken means the scrambled letters hold the vehicle inside them
dismissed suggests thrown out of order, so the letters of blame I are rearranged

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off blame after taking a bus to a famous African ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' gives AIMBEL. Abu Simbel is the Egyptian temple site of Rameses II, moved in the 1960s to escape the waters of the Aswan dam.
explanation.definitionFit: This pair of rock-cut temples in southern Egypt is a celebrated ancient monument in Africa.

clue.text: Petty cash running short unfortunately? Always in the same position

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder
running short means the word cash is cut off before its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone laments that the office petty cash is running low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running short' trims CASH to CAS; PETTY plus CAS is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor so cast is always given the same kind of role, stuck in one slot.

clue.text: Fight pointless battles, having inclination to take on flour suppliers?

definitions.meaning: to attack imaginary enemies or causes not worth fighting, as Don Quixote did

definitions.text: having inclination to take on flour suppliers?
definitions.meaning: read literally: tilting (an inclination) to attack the mills that grind flour

explanation.surface: Someone keen to pick fights with millers is wasting effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Quixote charged at windmills he took for giants. A tilt is an inclination, and to tilt at is to attack with a lance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom from Cervantes means attacking imaginary foes or hopeless causes.

clue.text: Indian believer is turning up in European capital

indicators.note: turning up means flipped over in a down clue, so the word is inside the capital is reversed in place

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A believer from India appears in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up in' is the signal: the clue's own word 'is' names the stretch of the capital to be flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Zoroastrian community of India, descended from Persian refugees, is a religious believer.

clue.text: Little thanks received by study on male function

indicators.note: received by means taken in by, so the thanks goes inside the study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
ta is a short informal word for thanks
a gent is a man, a male

explanation.surface: A man studying receives little gratitude for his efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: This trigonometric ratio, the reciprocal of tangent, is a mathematical function.

clue.text: Get out of money

definitions.meaning: to withdraw from a contest, as a horse withdrawn from a race
slang for cash, as in earning some readies

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is pulling out of a competition; the other is a slang word for cash.

clue.text: End of war captured in four outrageous lines? That's excessive

indicators.note: captured in means one piece is held inside another, here the end of war inside the rearranged number
outrageous means wild, so the letters of four are scrambled

parts.note: VE Day (Victory in Europe) marked the end of the Second World War in Europe
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Four outrageous lines of verse about the end of a war, it is suggested, go too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of war' looks like a call for the letter R, but means VE Day, Victory in Europe. 'outrageous' makes ORFU, and 'captured in' places the pair after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crammed beyond capacity is more than enough, so the clue's comment on excess fits.

clue.text: Apart from one time, Del Boy, say, returned a bit of repartee

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the trimmed surname is read backwards
apart from means without, so a letter is removed from the surname

parts.note: Del Boy is Derek Trotter of the British TV sitcom Only Fools and Horses; say marks him as an example of a Trotter
T is the abbreviation for time, and only one of the two is dropped

explanation.surface: A cheeky comeback from the sitcom wheeler-dealer Del Boy is quoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy is Derek Trotter, the market trader in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses. 'Apart from one time' drops one T, giving TROTER, and 'returned' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, witty reply is the very stuff that quick verbal exchange is made of.

clue.text: Over-optimistic, wordy, lacking power

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken away from the synonym

parts.note: prosy means dull and long-winded, wordy
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A critique of a forecast: too hopeful, too long-winded, too feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: A view seen through tinted glasses is cheerfully hopeful, perhaps more than the facts warrant.

clue.text: Independent gallery accepting a means of hanging picture back from European country

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the gallery's name opens to hold the other letters

parts.note: the Tate is a group of London art galleries

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the picture-hanging item is reversed

parts.note: a picture hangs on a nail in the wall

explanation.surface: An independent gallery hangs a picture brought back from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives LIAN, and 'accepting' places it with A after the gallery's first letter. The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes style borrowed from Italy, so the thing seems to come from that Mediterranean land.

clue.text: Weapon's thwarted greeting?

parts.note: to cross someone is to thwart them
a bow is a greeting made by bending the body

explanation.surface: A weapon is pictured as a greeting that has been snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval missile launcher fires bolts and is plainly a weapon.

clue.text: Source of habits? Observed adopting nastier ones at first

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the observed word wraps around the others

parts.note: saw means observed
viler means nastier

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of ones is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is seen picking up worse habits early on.
explanation.walkthrough: Savile Row is the London street famous for bespoke tailoring; a habit is a garment, as worn by a monk or rider.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street of tailors supplies fine clothing, and a habit is an outfit.

clue.text: Good article about Old English writer

indicators.note: about here simply places the article around the preceding letters' end, standing after them

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A good piece of writing about Old English is credited to an author.
explanation.definitionFit: The German author of Faust is one of the great writers of European literature.

clue.text: Giving basics to Shakespearean theatregoer missing line

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: groundlings stood in the pit at the Globe theatre in Shakespeare's time

explanation.surface: A standing playgoer at the Globe, missing a line, gets a lesson in fundamentals.
explanation.walkthrough: Groundlings were the poorest spectators, standing in the yard of Elizabethan playhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone thoroughly in the fundamentals of a subject is to teach them its foundations.

clue.text: Southern resort, beside Lake, has something to shift sand, perhaps

parts.note: Hove is a seaside resort beside Brighton in southern England

explanation.surface: A holiday spot on the south coast next to a lake has a spade for the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is an English seaside resort on the Sussex coast, next to Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-bladed digging tool moves loose material such as sand, so it fits the example given.

clue.text: Comedian, one writing dully about sergeant?

indicators.note: about means around, so the writer surrounds the soldier

parts.note: a hack is a writer of dull, routine work
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A comic is a dull scribbler writing about a sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Hancock was a British comedian of radio and TV's Hancock's Half Hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony of that surname was a famous British comic of the 1950s and 1960s.

clue.text: Sadly not done around one — or an hour earlier

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the numeral
sadly signals a sorry state, so the letters of not done are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a task left undone at around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' does double duty in the surface: it is the I inside, and one o'clock less an hour points to twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour before one o'clock is midday, and this old word names that time.

clue.text: Author's daughter becomes ill, not son

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for son is removed

parts.note: sickens means falls ill

explanation.surface: A writer's daughter falls ill while the son stays well.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles of that surname wrote Oliver Twist and is a great Victorian novelist.

clue.text: Some European he maligns misguidedly? Little new in that

indicators.note: in that means the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
misguidedly means wrongly directed, so the letters of he maligns are jumbled

parts.note: N is the short form, a little version, of new

explanation.surface: A European who badmouths others is mistaken, with little new to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from England is one particular kind of European.

clue.text: Urban amenity visionary put in place around capital of Wales

indicators.note: put in place around means the visionary is set around the letter

parts.note: a seer is a visionary prophet

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter, the capital letter, of Wales

explanation.surface: A prophet installs a civic facility around the Welsh capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Wales' looks like Cardiff, but it is only the letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground drainage for waste water is a basic public facility in a town.

clue.text: Channel avoided on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: ducked means dodged or avoided

explanation.surface: A radio channel is said to have been avoided.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube or pipe that carries air or fluid is a channel.

clue.text: End of one was indication to set up two

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised so it reads bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: cued means gave a signal or indication to

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of one

explanation.surface: The end of one thing signalled the start of a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' and 'two' tempt as numbers; two is the definition, the old word for a two on dice or cards.
explanation.definitionFit: On dice or playing cards the side or card bearing a pair of pips is called this.

clue.text: Regret a lot of vexed argument

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the synonym loses its last letter

parts.note: sore means annoyed, vexed
a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: Someone rues a great deal of bad-tempered quarrelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief or sadness over something is close in sense to regret, both meaning distress.

clue.text: This is certain to be encompassed by interpretation of 'idle'

definitions.text: This is certain to be encompassed by interpretation of 'idle'

indicators.note: to be encompassed by means to be surrounded, so the synonym goes inside the rearranged word
an interpretation of a word reads it differently, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A claim about what any reading of the word idle is sure to include.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: idleness is a fair interpretation of having plenty of free time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with ample free time and no need to work is idle in the relaxed sense.

clue.text: Broadcaster with lots of cash keeping source of revenue up

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the cash wraps around a letter

parts.note: wads are thick rolls of banknotes, lots of cash

indicators.note: source of means the start, so the first letter of revenue is taken

explanation.surface: A rich broadcaster protects its income stream as profits rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving toward the heavens means heading upward, so the adverb can stand for the direction up.

clue.text: Being ingratiating is not difficult with old king

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
easy means not difficult

explanation.surface: Flattering an elderly monarch turns out to be simple.
explanation.walkthrough: GR, Georgius Rex, is the royal cipher of the kings named George.
explanation.definitionFit: An oily, fawning manner is figuratively slippery, which is how flatterers come across.
